blocks.text: Sharding (horizontal partitioning) splits a dataset across multiple independent databases, each holding a subset of rows. You shard when a single primary can't handle the **write throughput** or the **data volume** — replicas only help reads. Each shard is usually itself replicated.
The price is real: cross-shard queries, joins and transactions become hard, rebalancing is operationally risky, and a bad shard key creates hot spots that defeat the whole point.

head: Good shard key property
Why
rows: Enough distinct values to spread across many shards
No single value gets a disproportionate share of traffic
Most queries hit one shard (e.g. all of a user's data on one shard)
Changing a row's key means moving it between shards

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.text: Sharding by timestamp or an auto-increment id with range partitioning: all new writes go to the last shard.

cols.title: Hash (mod N)
cons: Changing N reshuffles almost every key

cols.title: Consistent hashing
pros: Adding a node moves ~1/N of keys
cons: Still no range scans; more complex

cols.title: Directory / lookup table
pros: Any mapping you like; move tenants individually
cons: Lookup service is a dependency and must be cached

blocks.text: Hash both nodes and keys onto a ring of 2^32 positions. A key belongs to the first node clockwise from it. When a node joins, it takes over only the keys between it and its predecessor; when it leaves, only its keys move to the next node. Giving each physical node many **virtual nodes** spreads its share around the ring so load stays even.

sections.title: Routing a query to the right shard

items: Single-shard queries (include the shard key) are fast and scale linearly.
Scatter-gather queries (no shard key) hit every shard and are as slow as the slowest — avoid them on hot paths, or maintain a secondary index / search index.
**Joins:** denormalise, or co-locate related data on the same shard by sharing the shard key.
**Transactions:** avoid cross-shard transactions; use sagas, or a database with distributed transactions (Spanner, CockroachDB) when you must.
**Global secondary indexes:** a separate index table sharded by the indexed value (DynamoDB GSIs) — updated asynchronously.
**Unique constraints:** enforce on the shard key, or via a separate uniqueness table.

items.title: Pre-split
items.text: Start with many logical shards (e.g. 4,096) mapped onto a few physical servers; move logical shards later.

items.title: Copy
items.text: Stream the moving shard to the new host (snapshot + replication log).

items.title: Cut over
items.text: Briefly pause writes to the shard, catch up, flip the routing map.

items.title: Clean up
items.text: Delete the old copy after verification.

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: I'd shard by user_id with consistent hashing over many virtual shards, so most queries are single-shard and adding capacity only moves a fraction of the data. Hot celebrity keys get special handling — caching or splitting.
